## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by small cells divided into two symmetrical semicells by a deep central constriction. Staurastrum margaritaceum typically has four to six short, radiating arm-like processes on each semicell, with rows of tiny granules that give the cell wall an ornamented appearance. It occurs primarily in acidic, nutrient-poor freshwater habitats such as bog pools, peatlands, and shallow wetlands, often in association with Sphagnum. Like many desmids, it is associated with relatively clean, oligotrophic waters and contributes to freshwater primary production while also serving as an indicator of aquatic habitat conditions.
